newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: IATA calls emergency talks on Nov 13 on fuel costs.
newsitem.headline: IATA calls emergency talks on Nov 13 on fuel costs.

text.p: The International Air Transport Association (IATA) has called an emergency meeting of its 250 member airlines on November 13 to consider "concerted action" to counter rising fuel costs, an IATA spokesman said on Tuesday.
The spokesman said IATA airlines could decide on passenger fare and cargo rate increases at the talks being held in Geneva, or may elect to absorb the 10 per cent rise so far this year.
"They will consider the need for concerted action to counter the increase in the fuel cost burden. It could mean a fare and rate increase," he told Reuters. "It is an emergency situation."
"Fuel costs have been going up pretty steadily this year," IATA spokesman Tim Goodyear told Reuters.
The average worldwide price of fuel paid by IATA members during the first nine months of this year was U.S. 73.9 cents per U.S. gallon, against U.S. 65.2 cents in 1995, he added.
Internationally scheduled services spend $13 billion a year on aviation fuel, according to the IATA spokesman in Geneva.
"If the fuel price goes up 10 per cent, that is an extra $1.3 billion compared with airlines profits last year of $5.2 billion," Goodyear said.
